audit.why: Level 6 is genuinely Azir's (Emperor's Divide). The first-item and two-item rows are where a 58.8% win rate has to come from: Rod of Ages plus a permanent stardust curve, against a 22-second shield-dash that only covers one window.
audit.corrected: phases[4].side to 'Azir' (matching win[4]); phases[5].side and win[5] both to 'Aurelion Sol'; phases[6].side and win[6] both to 'Aurelion Sol'. audit.corrected: Rekeyed to The Skies Descend and stacked stardust with the real range.

audit.corrected: spikes[1], mid, breakdown.cooldowns and dontsFull[2] now carry the knockback-cancels-channel rule; dosFull[1] uses the no-soldier-no-dash window.

audit.why: Shifting Sands is 22s at rank 1 — the same clock as Astral Flight, which makes the pair easy to track together — and Emperor's Divide is 120s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with both clocks and the knockback note.

edits.before: Azir wins by landing Shifting Sands, denying your pattern, and owning the spacing war until your tempo starves.
edits.after: Azir wins by holding soldiers between you and the wave, then knocking your channel apart with Emperor's Divide.

edits.before: - Azir Shifting Sands: matchup-defining — His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. Check it before every step-up. - W Astral Flight is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Azir Shifting Sands: 22s at rank 1 — a shielded dash to a soldier, so step up in the window after he burns it. - Astral Flight runs the same 22s clock; chip damage never gets it. - Emperor's Divide: 120s, and its knockback cancels your channel.

edits.before: Carry by scaling honestly — every stardust stack is permanent, and the 30-minute version of you wins fights your laning self cannot imagine.
edits.after: Carry off his soldier line: the black hole sits where his soldiers must stand to hit you, and every second he lingers there is permanent stardust.

edits.before: W-flyby: fly a lateral arc, drag Q across Azir for two seconds of burn + stacks, and land outside his answer range — repeat forever from one item.
edits.after: Shifting Sands needs a soldier to dash to, so when his soldiers are on the wave and not on you, that is the 22-second window where he cannot leave.

edits.before: Channelling Q face-to-face inside his engage range with W down — every champion that touches you wins that exchange pre-items.
edits.after: Flying at him with Emperor's Divide up is a free knockback: the displacement ends the flight early and drops you behind his soldier line.

edits.before: Your first item narrows the trade gap but his shield and zoning still generally win exchanges
edits.after: Rod of Ages plus stacked stardust flips the trade: his 22s shield-dash covers only one window

edits.before: Both champions scale into real threats late, so late-game outcomes come down to play skill, not a clean stat edge
edits.after: Two items of permanent stardust and a 1250-range drag beat soldier zoning once fights start in earnest

edits.before: Emperor's Divide can shove you into his soldiers or away from allies, giving him full control over any skirmish near his wall.
edits.after: Emperor's Divide knocks back from 250 range, and that displacement cancels your beam and your flight outright — 120s at rank 1.

edits.before: Your first item's burst starts closing the trade gap, but Azir's shield and soldier zoning still make engages risky.
edits.after: Rod of Ages closes the trade gap: Shifting Sands is 22s, so outside that window his soldiers are all he has.

edits.before: With two items your Comet threat and 5-star ultimate can match his teamfight shove, but this stays a close, skill-dependent matchup, not a clean win.
edits.after: With two items The Skies Descend drags his whole formation in from 1250, and stacked stardust melts what Emperor's Divide was meant to protect.

edits.before: Azir's soldiers let him poke and zone from a range that outclasses your early Q, and his shield can straight-up block your star's damage on a well-timed cast. He controls the wave state easily, forcing you to either miss CS or eat chip damage every time you step up. Play patient, farm off your own Q star from max range when you can, and don't contest his zoning directly before you have levels or items to answer it.
edits.after: Azir's soldiers poke from a range that outclasses your 750 beam, and Shifting Sands both shields him and dashes him to a soldier, so his answer to your step-up is already placed. He controls the wave state easily, forcing you to miss CS or eat chip every time you walk up. Play patient, beam from max range, and don't contest his zoning before you have the levels or the item to answer it.

edits.before: Emperor's Divide is one of the best positional-control ultimates in the game, letting him wall you off from allies or shove you into his own soldiers for a pick. You're still working from behind here — his shield and soldier spacing continue to win most direct trades. Play around vision near walls, don't get caught in a spot where his ult can isolate you, and rely on jungler assistance rather than solo pressure.
edits.after: Emperor's Divide only casts at 250 range, but the knockback cancels whatever you are channelling and the wall then cuts you from your team. You're still working from behind — his 22-second shield-dash and soldier spacing win most direct trades. Hold the beam until he has committed the wall, don't stand where it can isolate you, and lean on jungler pressure rather than solo trades.

edits.before: Your first item narrows the damage gap, and by two items your global Comet and 5-star ultimate genuinely threaten to match his teamfight shove-and-zone control. This stays a close matchup even at full build, though — Azir's positional ultimate and soldier zoning don't fall off, so outcomes hinge on who plays cooldowns and positioning better rather than one side simply outscaling the other. Group fights around vision control and force him to commit Divide early.
edits.after: Rod of Ages narrows the damage gap, and by two items The Skies Descend pulls his whole formation into a beam he cannot walk his soldiers out of. His zoning does not fall off — Emperor's Divide still cuts a fight in half at 120 seconds — so the win comes from making him spend the wall on the wrong target, then holding the black hole exactly where his soldiers have to stand to reach you. Group around vision and force that wall out early.

edits.before: Zone with soldier pokes and shield-block your Q star's damage
edits.after: Zone with soldier pokes and absorb your beam behind his shield
